messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api-us-east1 p99 latency > 12s and queue depth growing on gpu-serving queue. autoscaler errors: "provisioner rate limit exceeded". link: https://grafana.redwood/example-dashboard?s=3812345600
rafael (oncall): acked. I'm looking at the queue now. p95 ~ 1.2s -> 3.8s -> spike to 10s in last 3m. tail requests timing out.
maya (sre): seeing the same. autoscaler logs show OOM of kube-provisioner and 429s from cloud API: 
```
2026-03-15T03:01:22Z provisioner ERROR: quotaExceeded: API rate limits - createInstance failed
2026-03-15T03:02:01Z autoscaler WARN: pending pods 420 -> 1200, no new nodes due to quota
```
rafael (oncall): current backlog on hosted queue: 18k requests, growth +2.5k/min. customer impact: timeouts for some low-tier customers, heavy traffic from one client app (unknown customer-id in logs) flooding short-text endpoints.
josh (infra): paging cloud provider support, but ETA on quota bump ~ 30m. Could we failover traffic to ded pool?
anya (ml-oncall): we can route <small-model> fallback to CPU-backed endpoints temporarily. It'll increase token latency but reduce GPU consumption. Suggest steps: 1) enable model fallback policy for short-text routes 2) start emergency ded pool if quota arrives.
ben (sre-lead): prioritize 1) immediate customer-facing mitigation (throttle, fallback), 2) stabilize autoscaler/provisioner, 3) postmortem + CS comms.
rafael (oncall): executing quick mitigations now: throttling top 5 noisy API keys by 80% (temporary). command run: `rbctl quota apply --keys-file noisy_keys.txt --qps 2`
maya (sre): also enabling prefix/KV cache bypass for large conversations to avoid extra GPU cycles. applied rule: `route:short-text -> fallback-model:small-cpu` in routing config.
ops-bot: Deployment notice: routing config change applied by rafael at 03:04:12Z.
josh (infra): cloud support responded: "we see your request spikes; quota increase request in progress, no guarantees. API limit reset window 8m for current token; you can request emergency higher priority." Calling partner rep now.
leah (cust-succ): I'm pulling the list of customers with elevated error rates. Will prepare outbound note for customers hitting >5% errors.
anya (ml-oncall): think we should also enable adaptive batching limit decrease to reduce per-request kernel memory pressure. I pushed an override: `inference.runtime.batch.max_tokens=256`
rafael (oncall): good. I also turned on fallback routing for the global short-text endpoint: 40% traffic to small-cpu, 60% to gpu for now.
ben (sre-lead): record decision: routing fallback + selective throttling + batch limit override. Reduce tail latencies and stall new provisioning to avoid further API calls while cloud rate limit heals.
maya (sre): autoscaler/provisioner still logging: `provisioner: instanceCreateFail quotaExceeded`. We attempted to spin 50 nodes; only 6 succeeded.
josh (infra): as a temporary measure we can free up some internal reserved capacity by deallocating test-dedicated pools. Doing `rb infra pool drain --name test-dedicated-eu --force` in 30s.
rafael (oncall): pagerduty: acknowledged (PD #INC-8765). tagging @ben for escalation if we don't see backlog flatten in 6m.
ops-bot: Metric update: backlog growth rate dropped from +2.5k/min to +300/min after throttles and fallback. p95 improved from 10s -> 2.8s. p99 still ~9s.
leah (cust-succ): initial customer list: cust-421, cust-812, cust-199 showing >7% 5xx. Drafting message: "We're investigating elevated errors and latencies in US region; temporary mitigations applied. We'll follow up with ETA." Will wait for SRE confirmation before sending.
anya (ml-oncall): logs show heavy GPU KV cache misses for 1 model variant from cust-421 traffic pattern. That client is sending many short unique prompts causing low cache hit. Could throttle by request rate per key.
rafael (oncall): throttles in place for top noisy keys. Monitoring queue.
maya (sre): observed a provisioning loop: provisioner retried creates fast -> hit rate limit -> exponential backoff not kicking in because controller misreads 429 as recoverable and retries more aggressively. Filing tactical patch: add 429 backoff gate.
ben (sre-lead): prioritize that fix post-incident, but for now maintain routing and throttles. Any opt-outs from customer success?
leah (cust-succ): cust-421 reached out on Slack, requesting priority; suggest temporary exception to avoid SLA breach? They are on mid-tier. They accept degraded small-model fallback for 10 minutes.
josh (infra): cloud rep authorized a one-time emergency create for +20 GPUs (expected provision 6-8m). I kicked off the request.
ops-bot: Event: emergency capacity requested at 03:12:44Z.
rafael (oncall): once new capacity arrives, we'll gradually shift traffic back: rollout plan -> 10% steps every 30s, monitor p99 and errors.
maya (sre): new nodes started arriving at 03:18:30Z (6 nodes). provisioning logs show some successes.
ops-bot: Metric update: backlog now 6k, p95 1.1s, p99 3.9s.
anya (ml-oncall): after routing revert test: small-cpu route handling stable. We'll keep fallback rule at 25% for 15m to observe.
ben (sre-lead): handoff note for second shift: summarize mitigations + TODOs. Rafael, please prepare handoff in 10m for oncoming oncall.
rafael (oncall): preparing handoff: current state -> backlog 5.7k, throttles active for keys [cust-421,cust-812,cust-199], fallback 25% on short-text, emergency capacity 6 nodes active. Autoscaler still logging 429s but clouds quota token recovering. PD incident remains open.
leah (cust-succ): sent interim update to impacted customers at 03:25Z. Template: "We've applied throttles and fallbacks; some requests may see degraded responses. We'll update once capacity stabilizes."
ben (sre-lead): next steps: 1) postmortem (owner: maya), 2) add 429 backoff gate to provisioner (owner: josh), 3) throttle policy improvements + noisy-key auto-detection (owner: anya), 4) customer comms followup (owner: leah).
rafael (oncall): handing off to night oncall @maya in 10m. If backlog starts trending up again revert to full throttle and raise to ben.
maya (sre): ack. I'll take it. Leaving a short runbook in ops-pager: 
```
- Watch hosted queue backlog and p99
- If backlog > 8k -> escalate to ben and enable global rate-shed 50%
- If autoscaler logs persist 429 -> stop aggressive retries: `rbctl provisioner pause-retries`
- Contact cloud rep for further quota increases
```
ops-bot: Incident timeline updated. Incident ticket: INC-8765.
rafael (oncall): handoff complete. thanks all.
maya (sre): closing slack thread for now, will update if anything regresses.
